solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feckless types in front hog broadcast, entering property

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go into the word for property, splitting it before its last letter

parts.note: goods are possessions, a person's property

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Idle louts pile into a house while a pig gets talked about on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio talk but scatters the letters; 'entering' slips them in just before the final S of the word for property.
explanation.definitionFit: Feckless means lacking purpose or energy, and the plural noun names worthless idlers of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Apparently amateur plans for lightweights

indicators.note: an amateur is the opposite of a pro, so the word for plans, apparently made amateur, loses its leading professional

parts.note: programmes are schedules or plans of action

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that someone's schemes look like the work of a dabbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently amateur' takes PRO, the professional, off the front of PROGRAMMES; 'apparently' admits the joke is a pretend etymology.
explanation.definitionFit: Metric units of mass this small are tiny weights, so they are literally light weights.

clue.text: Gold real estate round site of Walt Disney World

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
real estate is land and property
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A golden property deal surrounding the famous Florida theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city hosts the Walt Disney World resort on its south-west edge, so it is that park's location.

clue.text: Don joining rep, possibly 18

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, also called a fellow of a college
a sales rep is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: An Oxford academic signs up with a salesman, perhaps out of political sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is PARTISAN; 'possibly' warns that the answer is only one kind of partisan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sympathiser of a political cause, classically communism, without being a party member is one sort of partisan supporter.

clue.text: Stagger, having got up in plant

parts.note: to stagger is to sway or rock
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: Someone totters after climbing to their feet in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Cistus and helianthemum shrubs go by this common name, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Opening (not large) in unit in factory, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the shortened opening goes inside the word for unit

parts.note: one is the unit number

indicators.note: not here means the letter for large is left out of the word for opening

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A small gap appears in a section of a factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to drop the large size from the narrow opening, and 'in' places what remains inside the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done at the place itself, such as a factory, is said to happen at the location rather than elsewhere.

clue.text: Poach it twice, claiming right to break well-known pledge

indicators.note: claiming means the doubled words take in the letter for right
to break the letters is to smash them into a new order
twice says the two words are taken two times over

parts.note: the words as written, used as letters

explanation.surface: A cook is told to poach something twice, and to break with convention while doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles POACH IT, 'claiming' adds R, and 'to break' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors traditionally swore this ethical oath, the most famous professional vow, named after a Greek physician.

clue.text: Get up on horse, but not quite — it's quite a height

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the reversed word sits above the trimmed horse
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to get is to gain

indicators.note: not quite means the horse's name stops one letter short

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Someone tries to mount a horse but can't quite manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' looks like mounting, but 'up' turns the synonym for get upside down in this down clue; 'not quite' trims the last letter of the horse breed, placed below ('on').
explanation.definitionFit: The famous falls on the US-Canada border drop about fifty metres, a considerable height for a waterfall.

clue.text: Dubious conjecture briefly ousting one in action

indicators.note: ousting means the short guess pushes out and replaces the numeral

parts.note: a suit is a legal action
I is the Roman numeral for one
spec, short for speculation, is a conjecture or guess

explanation.surface: A shaky theory, quickly summarised, removes someone from active duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' puts SPEC in place of the I in SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something questionable or of doubtful reliability can be called this, as in a doubtful-looking package.

clue.text: Book too late for dance and miss second team

indicators.note: too late means the book's letter arrives at the end of the dance instead of the start

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
to miss something is to lack it

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a dance too late and so misses the second team's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too late' shifts B from the front of BALL to the back, making ALLB. The team is New Zealand's national rugby union side.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand's national rugby union side, named for its dark kit, is a famous sporting team.

clue.text: Culminates in verbal outbursts of anger

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: piques are fits of resentment or irritation

explanation.surface: A quarrel comes to a head in shouted fits of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To culminate is to reach a high point, and the verb meaning to reach a maximum says the same.

clue.text: Height indicated by floor number, in a somewhat roundabout way

indicators.note: a roundabout way here means the extracted letters are read in the reverse direction
somewhat means only part of the phrase is taken, letters lifted from inside it

explanation.surface: A lift shows how high you are by the floor number, though by an indirect route.
explanation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, one of several hill classes in this puzzle. 'somewhat' lifts ORNUM from 'floor number' and 'roundabout way' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish peak above 3,000 feet is a height in the hill-walking sense, a named summit.

clue.text: Judicious English principle

parts.note: judicious means sensible, rational

explanation.surface: A sensible English rule of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The reasoning or underlying basis behind a course of action is its fundamental principle.

clue.text: Silence surrounding model, back on bed, showing tongue

indicators.note: surrounding means the call for silence goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: back means the word for model is read backwards

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's model lies on a bed in hushed silence, sticking her tongue out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the posing word round; 'on' in an across clue puts it after the bed, and 'surrounding' wraps the hush around both.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots Gaelic and Scots are languages, and a language is called a tongue.

clue.text: Fancied wee snifter about a quarter to? Not half

indicators.note: about means the small drink goes round the compass letter

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky
E, east, is one of the four compass quarters

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the little word is used

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a small whisky at a quarter to the hour, and very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside DRAM. 'Not half' plays on the slang 'not half!' for 'very much', but here it keeps half of TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to imagine or fancy it, so the past tense means imagined.

clue.text: Jack-of-all-trades, using pointer, scores back to front

parts.note: a hand on a clock is a pointer

indicators.note: back to front means the last letter of the word for scores is brought round to its start

parts.note: scores of things are many of them

explanation.surface: A versatile workman uses a pointer and adds up the scores in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the Y of MANY to the front, giving YMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person able to do odd jobs and repairs of many kinds is a versatile all-rounder.

clue.text: Carp about, mostly freshwater fish, its remaining tail being eaten by pet

indicators.text: its remaining tail being eaten by
indicators.note: the fish's new final letter, left after trimming, is swallowed up by the pet that follows
mostly means the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: the pike is a predatory freshwater fish
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: An angler grumbles about a pike whose tail has been chewed off by the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like a fish beside the pike, but with 'about' it is the definition. 'mostly' docks the fish, then 'its remaining tail being eaten by' tucks its new last letter inside the pet, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault, and the phrasal verb means to nag or criticise in petty ways.

clue.text: Animal killer — sanctimonious or rogue? — somewhere in between

indicators.note: somewhere in between means the rogue sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious
a cad is a rogue

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer asks whether a bullring killer is holier-than-thou or a scoundrel, and decides he is somewhere in between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is used as written, and 'somewhere in between' slots the rogue between the pious word and it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bullfight this mounted lancer wounds the bull, so he takes part in killing an animal.

clue.text: Gentleman Jim sitting centrally in my punt

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation like 'my!'
a punt is a bet

indicators.note: centrally means the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer called Gentleman Jim sits in the middle of my flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' is a wager, not a boat. 'centrally' takes the middle letter of 'sitting', which ends the answer. A Corbett is also a Scottish hill, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: James J. Corbett, the American heavyweight boxing champion of the 1890s, was nicknamed Gentleman Jim.

clue.text: After start of project, craftsman becomes biased

indicators.note: after means the craftsman comes after the first letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: Once a project gets going, the craftsman shows a bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strongly committed to one side or party is prejudiced, one-sided, not impartial.

clue.text: Compassion half given on driving test about sign

indicators.note: given on means the reversed test is placed after the half-word, below it in a down clue
half means only the first four of its eight letters are used

parts.note: sympathy is compassion

indicators.note: about means the word for the test is turned round

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A driving examiner shows only half-hearted compassion, a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for cars; 'about' makes it TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is an indication of illness, and more generally any indication or sign of something.

clue.text: Characters saunter about

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: Odd people stroll around the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's essential qualities make up their character, so the plural means personalities or dispositions.

clue.text: Good Martha taking time out for dancing. This one did!

definitions.text: Good Martha taking time out for dancing. This one did!

indicators.note: for dancing means the remaining letters jig about into a new order
taking, paired with out, means the letter for time is removed from the name
out completes the instruction to remove the letter for time from the name

explanation.surface: A tribute to Martha, the great choreographer, who certainly did take time out to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking time out' drops T from MARTHA and 'for dancing' rearranges MARHA. Martha Graham was the pioneering American modern dancer; a Graham is also a Scottish hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha Graham, the American modern-dance pioneer, is the dancer the clue says actually danced.

clue.text: Perhaps one of many on flight 16, an alien Pole

definitions.text: Perhaps one of many on flight

parts.note: 16 across means find fault, and so does carp
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, is an alien
a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: An alien Pole on a plane is one of many who complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a flight of stairs, not a plane trip; 16 is PICK AT, which equals CARP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair carpet is held in place by a metal bar at each step, so a staircase has many of them.

clue.text: Company dealt with high-flier

parts.note: to meet a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A firm handled its star executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A celestial body with a glowing tail streaks across the sky, so it literally flies high.

clue.text: Remain hollow when fed by wife

indicators.note: fed by means the letter for wife goes into the hollow

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow

explanation.surface: Someone stays in a little valley while his wife brings him food.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger or stay put somewhere, or to reside, is to remain there.

clue.text: Third-rate artiste overacting when given more stout

parts.note: ham acting is overacting
stouter means fatter

explanation.surface: A bad performer hams it up even more after putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: This old theatre slang names a poor, ranting performer, from minstrels who greased their make-up with lard.

clue.text: Retreats occupied by human beings, the older members primarily being housed

definitions.text: Retreats occupied by human beings, the older members primarily being housed

indicators.note: occupied by means the word for retreats is filled with the other pieces

parts.note: to retreat is to retire or withdraw
men are human beings

indicators.note: being housed means the initials sit inside the little word before them
primarily means the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Care homes are places where people live, the elderly first and foremost being looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: 'primarily' takes initials of 'older members', 'being housed' sets them inside 'the', and 'occupied by' fills the word for retreats with that and the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Residences where elderly people live together and are cared for in old age are retreats for the old.
